records.subagent_summary: All 8 round-3 rollouts scored 0: six explicitly argued that a speaker who knows their own number plus the public number can compute the partner, concluded both the sum reading and the product reading are impossible, and then emitted an arbitrary divisor of the public number to fill the answer box (three separate divisors appeared across the eight samples), while three burned the token cap looping on that same contradiction. The revision front-loads an explicit per-speaker knowledge inventory that forbids 'just subtract/divide', replaces group-deletion language with a concrete per-private-value count of partners across readings, and adds an explicit bar on guessing when every reading looks contradictory - the exact point where every failure went astray.

All 8 round-3 rollouts scored 1 (3.3k-7.7k tokens), so training is saturated and the loss is transfer: every rollout got |z-a|=k|z-b| within a few hundred tokens, but then 4 of 8 burned 12-40 exponential expressions re-deriving individual roots to spot-check the locus, and 3 of 8 (including the two most hedged, 16-18 'Wait's) stalled on a self-inflicted contradiction from testing the center point itself and concluding the circle was wrong. The revision therefore adds a portable constant-work route to the circle's data (the two collinear points where the bars drop, which bound a diameter, giving center as midpoint and radius as half the distance), demotes the coordinate expansion to a single cross-check, and states explicitly that the center is not on the circle so |z| varying is expected.

Round-3 training reproduced 7/8 with the incumbent; the single failure never ran the incumbent invariance test properly because it mis-listed the large square vertices and then evaluated the aligned orientation as full containment (overlap = whole small square) instead of the actual corner region, so its two test values disagreed and it settled on a verbally asserted rotated fraction with no computed region. Held-out also fell to 0.0875 under the incumbent, indicating its bespoke k-fold-wedge criterion is being applied by fiat rather than checked, while the round-2 shoelace variant lifted held-out to 0.2 but collapsed train. This revision therefore prepends a cheap coordinate/vertex audit and an explicit ban on uncomputed overlap fractions, keeps the invariance-then-stop control flow that trains well, and routes disagreement back to re-checking the region instead of a costly general clipping search.

My 8 public rollouts scored 6/8; both failures were token-cap truncations, never wrong answers. One never partitioned indices at all and burned the budget building a recursive shift construction from adjacent-term differences; the other quoted the hint's product late but then re-imposed a constant successive difference within a single polynomial's own values, concluded 'each function contributes at most one term', and looped. The revision therefore targets that specific trap: it states that a function's index group need not be consecutive so its own successive differences carry no information, and adds a discard rule for any line ending in 'P must be affine' or 'one term per function'.

Train fell to 5/8 with the incumbent. All three failures shared one root cause: after solving the reduced rational equation they assigned the translated vertex a y-value that does not satisfy the curve (P off the graph), and two of them noticed the contradiction, called the problem inconsistent, and reported the area anyway; the third burned its whole budget on a mis-fit parameter pair it never sanity-checked against the given points. The revision keeps the reduction pipeline but replaces the discriminant flip-and-redo advice with two cheap closures: re-derive the given points' y from the fitted parameters, and evaluate f at every new vertex before any area is computed.

My 8 rollouts under the incumbent scored 2/8; the two successes were the only ones that used the rule 'bottom of the shed is the first bag delivered' and then multiplied 1/2 per real branch point, while five failures assumed uniformity (1/24, 1/4 from 'each bag equally likely to be last') and one inverted the orientation to conclude the outcome was forced. Rounds 1-2 already showed that long enumerate-the-whole-tree hints hurt held-out badly, so this revision stays near the incumbent's length and adds only the two steps the successful rollouts used: translate the asked position into a delivery rank, then count genuine 1/2 branch points versus forced moves.

All 8 rollouts scored 0 with a single shared error: each set P(x)=sum_i a_i x^i and reinterpreted row k as P(k)=0, swapping the node index with the condition exponent; the resulting degree-2005 polynomial with only 2004 roots left one free parameter, so rollouts either stalled declaring the system inconsistent/underdetermined or resolved the free root arbitrarily and reported a harmonic-sum, 1/2005, or 0 value. Rounds 1-2 already tried longer prose warnings against that swap and lost heldout accuracy, so this revision drops the warning framing and instead gives the positive mechanical rule -- apply the rows to a test polynomial evaluated at the nodes, chosen to isolate one weight -- keeping the text near incumbent length since the shorter incumbent transfers best.

All 8 of my round-3 public rollouts scored reward 1 (train_i = 1.0), the third saturated round, so the only headroom is transfer, where the incumbent gets 9/80. Every correct rollout ran the same spine (divide-every-total -> gcd -> take max count -> sum -> scale by 1.2), and their only wasted effort was 6-23 backtracks re-deriving that the gcd is the maximum admissible count and re-reading the domain nouns; rounds 1 and 2 showed that replacing the incumbent with a longer, restructured generic paragraph (137 and 162 tokens) collapses train to 3/8 and 4/8 for only +2 and +3 heldout. So instead of another rewrite I made a minimal-delta edit at nearly the incumbent's length: same sentence skeleton and same operative phrases, but the house/street/construction nouns swapped for domain-neutral ones and the gcd-is-the-largest-N step stated explicitly, which should keep the training spine intact while letting the method apply to non-housing items of this class.

All 8 public rollouts were correct again this round (8/8, 3.8k-6.1k tokens, none truncated), so the training question is saturated and the only loss is transfer and wasted reasoning. Every rollout still burned its first ~800 tokens writing out the generic ax^3+bx^2+cx+d pair before recentering, and each re-derived the B=+-A branch and then argued from scratch about why B=-A, because the incumbent asserts the odd-n sign without a reason. The revision explicitly bans the generic-coefficient opening, supplies the reason (B=A collapses to p=q, which distinct given data forbids), and adds the read-off rule that the fixed point is free and an input at distance d costs only A*d^n, so evaluation needs no expansion; the round-2 attempt to widen the trigger to all polynomial functional identities cost train 5/8, so the p(q)=q(p) trigger is kept concrete.

4/8 correct: one failure asserted the composite of the overlapping block swaps was disjoint transpositions and answered 2 without ever tracing it, and the three length-capped failures thrashed because their position map disagreed with their own string simulation after they silently switched between "slot i receives" and "label at i goes to" (one produced a non-injective map with two positions sent to the same target and never noticed). Two of those reached self-consistent counts for the smallest sizes, then abandoned them and burned the remaining budget inventing piecewise formulas for different n instead of rechecking the smaller simulation.
